reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates a more targeted approach to building both aerobic endurance and hill strength – crucial elements for trail running performance. While both plans have similar overall duration, Plan A includes dedicated hill repeats and tempo runs, which directly address key speed and power development needs. Plan B’s focus almost entirely on long, easy runs, while beneficial for endurance, doesn’t provide the necessary stimulus for improving running economy or lactate threshold, which are vital for faster times.  Furthermore, Plan A’s inclusion of a strength session is a valuable addition for injury prevention and supporting the demands of trail running.
